title: Adam Air 574
summary: Adam Air Flight 574, a Boeing 737-400, crashed into the Makassar Strait on 1 January 2007 with all 102 people aboard killed. The flight crew became preoccupied with troubleshooting an inertial navigation system anomaly. While attempting to reset the IRS, the first officer inadvertently disconnected the autopilot, and neither pilot noticed the disconnect. The aircraft entered a slow right bank, and when the bank angle warning sounded, the crew did not recognize the autopilot disconnect and the aircraft entered an uncontrolled descent into the sea.
probable_cause: This accident resulted from a combination of factors, including the failure of the pilots to adequately monitor the aircraft following an inadvertent autopilot disconnect during IRS troubleshooting. Previous maintenance issues involving the aircraft's ailerons caused the airplane to slowly roll to the right, and the pilots did not notice or arrest the descent before impacting the sea.

factors.evidence: the first officer switched knob to Attitude mode causing autopilot to disengage with 4-second disconnect tone
Neither crew member noticed the autopilot was no longer engaged
Problems started when the pilots noticed an anomaly in the inertial reference system
the crew did not notice the autopilot disconnect tone while troubleshooting the IRS
When the aircraft reached 35 degree right bank and increasing, a bank angle audible warning sounded in the cockpit
The aircraft crashed into the Makassar Strait near Polewali

events.text: On 1 January 2007, at 12:59 local time, the plane departed from Juanda Airport, Surabaya, and climbed to cruise altitude.
Problems started when the pilots noticed an anomaly in the inertial reference system.
The first officer attempted to troubleshoot by resetting his IRS unit, switching the knob on his side to Attitude mode.
This disengaged the autopilot with a 4-second autopilot disconnect tone.
When the aircraft reached 35 degree right bank and increasing, a bank angle audible warning sounded in the cockpit.
The aircraft crashed into the Makassar Strait near Polewali in Sulawesi with all 102 people on board killed.

title: Kenya Airways 507
summary: The aircraft departed Douala at 00:06 local time without seeking takeoff clearance from the control tower. Once airborne, the aircraft developed a right bank tendency which the captain initially controlled. After 24 seconds at 1,000 feet, the captain let go of the control wheel and called for autopilot engagement, but the first officer did not acknowledge the command and the autopilot did not engage. For 55 seconds neither pilot nor autopilot controlled the aircraft, which gradually increased its bank angle to 34 degrees when the bank angle warning sounded. The captain's corrective inputs aggravated the situation, and with the aircraft banking at 115 degrees right at 2,290 feet, the crew could not recover.
probable_cause: The aircraft departed without receiving clearance from air traffic control. The autopilot did not engage due to lack of acknowledgment from the copilot. The pilots failed to detect the increasing bank angle until it became critical, and used opposite and conflicting control inputs that prevented recovery.

factors.evidence: The pilot in command failed to seek takeoff clearance from the Airport Control Tower and the aircraft departed Douala at 00:06 local time
The captain called out 'Ok, command' to engage the autopilot, but this command was not read back by the first officer and there was no audio confirmation the autopilot had been engaged
The captain believed he had activated the autopilot after 42 seconds of flight, but the autopilot did not engage
Pilots did not notice that the aircraft was increasingly banking to the right, from less than 1 degree to 34 degrees when the bank angle warning came on
The captain made a series of movements on the control wheel first left, then 40 degrees right, then 11 degrees to the left, which only aggravated the situation
The first officer gave the control wheel near opposite commands to what the captain had done, and the two pilots used opposite and conflicting control inputs
During the captain's upgrade training, his instructors recorded deficiencies in crew resource management skills, adherence to standard operating procedures, and cockpit scan
The aircraft crashed at 287 knots at 48 degrees down pitch and 60 degrees right bank in an unrecoverable state

events.text: The pilot in command failed to seek takeoff clearance from the Airport Control Tower and the aircraft departed Douala
Once airborne, the plane had a tendency to bank right, which the captain countered by using his control wheel at 1,000 ft altitude
The captain let go of the control wheel and called out 'Ok, command' to engage the autopilot
The aircraft was banking at 34 degrees and the bank angle warning came on
The captain made a series of control movements left, then 40 degrees right, then 11 degrees left to correct the bank
With the plane banking at 50 degrees, the captain tried to bring it under control by using right rudder, causing it to bank further right
The first officer gave control wheel commands opposite to what the captain had done; the captain engaged the autopilot but the plane was already banked at 115 degrees right at 2,290 ft
The aircraft pitched nose down after reaching 2900 ft with a 115 degree right bank and crashed
